record.original_question: Is there a universal constant C such that every Boolean function f : {-1,1}^n -> {-1,1} satisfies H[\hat{f}^2] <= C * I[f], where H[\hat{f}^2] is the spectral entropy and I[f] is the total influence?

evidence.quote: Statement: There is a universal constant C such that for any f : {-1, 1}^n -> {-1, 1} it holds that H[ f-hat^2 ] <= C * I[ f ], where H[ f-hat^2 ] is the spectral entropy and I[ f ] is the total influence.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a Boolean function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, write its Fourier–Walsh expansion as
$$f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}}\hat{f}(S)\,\chi_S(x),\qquad \chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i,$$
with Fourier coefficients $\hat{f}(S)=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\{-1,1\}^n}[f(x)\chi_S(x)]$. By Parseval's identity, $\sum_S \hat{f}(S)^2 = 1$, so the squared Fourier coefficients form a probability distribution on subsets of $\{1,\dots,n\}$.

Define the spectral entropy of $f$ by
$$H[\hat{f}^2] \;=\; \sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}} \hat{f}(S)^2 \,\log_2\!\frac{1}{\hat{f}(S)^2},$$
with the convention $0\log(1/0)=0$, and define the total influence of $f$ by
$$I[f] \;=\; \sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}} |S|\,\hat{f}(S)^2.$$

Question: Does there exist a universal constant $C>0$ (independent of $n$ and of $f$) such that for every $n\ge 1$ and every Boolean function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$,
$$H[\hat{f}^2] \;\le\; C\cdot I[f]\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The Fourier Entropy–Influence conjecture of Friedgut and Kalai remains open as of 2025. Partial progress continues, including improved bounds (e.g., Han's 2025 Combinatorica paper bounding spectral entropy by O(I(f) + Σ I_k(f) log(1/I_k(f)))) and proofs for restricted classes of Boolean functions, but no universal linear bound H[f̂²] ≤ C·I[f] has been established.

status_evidence.title: A New Bound for the Fourier-Entropy-Influence Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: We give a new bound on the Fourier entropy of a Boolean function in terms of its influences, improving previous results.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2023/2025) work provides only an improved partial bound, not a full proof of the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Fourier-Entropy-Influence Conjecture overview
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture continues to serve as a focal point for research, with substantial progress but full resolution still elusive.
status_evidence.claim: The FEI conjecture is still open as of 2025.

status_evidence.title: On the Analysis of Boolean Functions and Fourier-Entropy-Influence Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of the FEI conjecture and related quantities.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on the FEI conjecture without resolution.
